---
name: usage-switch-account-logout-v301
description: Why Claude Usage's Switch Account opens claude.ai/logout and why the Google sign-in button used to be greyed out
metadata:
  type: project
---

v301.0 (2026-11-03, commit 7badb49, published): Claude Usage "Switch Account" navigates to https://claude.ai/logout (Daniel asked for "clica no sair"); the v300 account-menu flow was removed. The composer usage popup "Account:" now shows the Claude CLI account (.claude.json oauthAccount.emailAddress), not the usage page login — Daniel's explicit requirement.

**Why:** "Continue with Google" greyed out was NOT reproducible in a plain WebView2 or with any extension tweak; claude.ai's login disables it during its add/switch-account flow (locked e-mail), which the old menu-based Switch Account led into. Daniel confirmed Google worked in the Exp instance after a plain logout.

**How to apply:** if Google sign-in goes grey again, check whether something re-entered claude.ai's add-account flow before suspecting WebView2 detection (window.chrome.webview is telemetry only). Logout path NOT yet F5-verified by Daniel. Related: [[chat-localization-v269]].
commit 7badb49c7762a44af4b20379d8a074875856d282
Author: dliedke <dliedke@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Nov 3 09:12:08 2026 -0300

    v301.0: Switch Account logs out of claude.ai, popup shows the Claude Code account
    
    - Claude Usage "Switch Account" now opens claude.ai's own /logout link (the
      href of its "Log out" menu item) instead of opening the account menu. The
      menu's add-account login locks the e-mail and disables "Continue with
      Google". The shared cookie copy is deleted first so a rebuilt view does not
      sign back in; the Google session is kept. The switch-mode state (timer,
      cookie signature poll, Reload/redirect exceptions) is removed.
    - The composer usage popup's "Account:" line now shows the Claude CLI's own
      account (oauthAccount.emailAddress in .claude.json, per Windows/WSL side),
      read during the existing account sync, instead of the usage page's login.
    - Switch Account tooltip updated in all languages; tests for the e-mail
      parser and the logout link.

147:- Change Account in the `⚙` menu (v91.0, real `claude auth` calls in v112.0, WSL support in v113.0): the one 🤖-menu feature that got a real native implementation instead of being hidden. `ChangeAccountNativeMenuItem`/`ChangeAccountNativeSeparator` (own item, not the terminal's `ChangeAccountMenuItem`) are shown by `ProviderContextMenu_Opened` only when `IsNativeModeActive && IsClaudeProvider(...)`. `ChangeAccountNativeMenuItem_Click` (NativeChat.cs) can't script `/logout` into a TUI that doesn't exist headless — measured: the headless CLI rejects slash commands sent over the structured channel outright (`AskSideQuestionAsync`'s `/btw` comment: *"isn't available in this environment"*). The v91.0 fix opened `https://claude.ai` in the default browser and relied on the user switching there, but that never actually worked: a browser session against the web app is a completely separate credential store from the one the locally-run CLI authenticates with, so the relaunch always came back on the same cached account (issue reported as "switching doesn't work"). v112.0 replaces the browser-homepage step with the CLI's own non-interactive `claude auth logout` (awaited, clears the real local credential) followed by `claude auth login` (fire-and-forget — it drives its own OAuth round-trip in the browser and isn't killed by disposing the `Process` wrapper without `Kill()`). v112.0 shipped this unconditionally against `ResolveNativeClaudeExecutable()` (the Windows-side `claude.exe`) even for the `ClaudeCodeWSL` provider — but a native-mode `ClaudeCodeWSL` session's actual child process is `wsl.exe` (`ClaudeCommandBuilder.GetFileName`), authenticating against the distro's own `~/.claude.json`, a completely separate file from the Windows one. So the v112.0 handler logged out/in a Windows credential the running WSL conversation never used: no error, but the switch silently did nothing for WSL. v113.0 fixes this by branching on `isWsl = activeProvider == AiProvider.ClaudeCodeWSL` and running both subcommands as `wsl.exe bash -lic "claude auth logout"` / `"claude auth login"` instead. Still signs out the usage WebView2 first (`SignOutUsageWindowIfActiveAsync`, same as the terminal flow) and still waits for an OK on a message box before calling `RelaunchNativeSessionAsync` so the next turn's process launch picks up whatever credentials are current at that point. `auth login` needs a real console, unlike `auth logout` (also fixed v113.0): `claude auth login` drives an interactive OAuth round-trip — it prints the browser URL to stdout and, if the browser's own redirect can't complete automatically, asks the user to paste a code back into that same process's stdin. The original v112.0 `Process.Start` used `CreateNoWindow = true` for both subcommands; `auth logout` does no interactive I/O so that was harmless, but for `auth login` it meant the process had no console at all — no stdout to print the browser URL/prompt to, no stdin to read a pasted code from — so the browser never opened and login could never actually complete, even though the `Process.Start` call itself raised no exception (reported: "browser is not opening", "not showing new account after OK", "even a new chat doesn't show the account" — all three were downstream of this one root cause, since the account was never actually being set). Fixed by launching it through `cmd.exe /k` with `CreateNoWindow = false` (`cmd.exe /k "<claudeExe>" auth login`, or `cmd.exe /k wsl bash -lic "claude auth login"` for WSL) — the same `/k`-wrapped visible-console pattern the terminal launch itself uses elsewhere in `ClaudeCodeControl.Terminal.cs`, which gives the CLI a real window to print to and read from, and keeps that window open after the CLI exits so an error stays legible instead of flashing shut. `claude.ai` is opened in the browser again too, but before `auth login` now, not instead of it (v113.0): fixing the console alone was not enough — claude.ai's OAuth *authorize* endpoint has no account picker, so if the browser is already signed in as the old account, the CLI's login round-trip silently re-approves that same account through the existing session cookies, which is indistinguishable from "the switch did nothing". So the handler now opens plain `https://claude.ai` first and blocks on a message box asking the user to consciously sign out and into the desired account there — only after that confirmation does it run `claude auth login`, which then rides whatever account is now active in the browser. A second message box (reworded from the original "browser will open" text, since the browser step already happened) asks for confirmation once the CLI's own console-window flow (paste-a-code fallback included) is done, before `RelaunchNativeSessionAsync` fires
288:- Returning to the usage view after a manual account switch (v158.0): `TryRedirectToUsage`'s post-auth landing whitelist (`/new`, `/chats`, `/chat/`, `/projects`, `/recents`) deliberately excluded the root path, because `/` doubles as the signed-out home page and redirecting it unconditionally loops `/settings/usage → / → /settings/usage`. claude.ai drops a fresh sign-in on `/` about as often as on `/new`, so Switch Account → native "Log out" → sign in as a different user left the panel parked on the home page until the user pressed Refresh. `_sawSignedOutPage` (set whenever the embedded page visits `/login`, `/logout`, `/magic-link` or `/auth`) now promotes `/` to a landing, and `RedirectToUsageIfSettledAsync` requires a non-empty claude.ai `sessionKey` cookie (`HasClaudeSessionCookieAsync`) before navigating — a genuinely signed-out root reads no cookie and is left alone. The flag is cleared as the redirect fires, so a navigate that bounces straight back to `/` cannot re-arm it: one attempt per sign-out. The settle path re-checks `core.Source` both before and after the awaited cookie read, since the await gives the page another chance to move. `/onboarding` is deliberately *not* a landing — an account claude.ai forces through onboarding would ping-pong `/onboarding → /settings/usage` every ~6.5 s (1.5 s settle + 5 s debounce).
289:- Trim restore after Switch Account (`TryRestoreTrim`, v158.0): `SwitchAccountButton_Click` sets `window.__claudeSuppressTrim` so claude.ai's own chrome — and with it the account menu — stays visible. That flag lives on the document, so a full page load clears it by itself, but an SPA route change back to `/settings/usage` does not, leaving the raw settings page (sidebar and all) in the panel. Both `OnNavigationCompleted` and `OnSourceChanged` now clear the flag whenever the source is on `/settings/usage`, ahead of the redirect check.
290:- Following a Claude CLI account switch (v221.0): the bars come from the WebView2's own claude.ai session, which has nothing to do with the CLI's credentials, so `/logout` + `/login` typed into the terminal (or `claude auth login` anywhere) moved the agent to another account while the bars kept scraping, and refreshing, the old one. Only the ⚙ "Change Account" items signed the page out. `SyncUsageWithClaudeAccountAsync` runs on every background tick (ahead of the foreground-tab guard) and once before the startup refresh. It reads `oauthAccount` from the active side's `~/.claude.json` (the distro's copy for `ClaudeCodeWSL`, with the `wslpath` result cached per session). `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is honored on both sides (`GetClaudeJsonPath`, `${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME}` under WSL), because the CLI then keeps the file in that folder and never writes the one in the home directory. It identifies the account as `accountUuid/organizationUuid`, so switching organizations under the same login counts as a switch too, since usage limits are per organization. It falls back to the e-mail address when the UUIDs are missing. No `oauthAccount` (between `/logout` and `/login`) or a half-written file reads as "unknown" and never as a switch. The account the page was last paired with is kept per side (`windows`/`wsl`) in `usage-account.json` next to the settings, not in the settings. Every VS window saves its whole in-memory settings on each scrape, so a second window would write the old account back and then sign the shared page out a second time. The first check on a side only records the account. A window can find the pairing already moved to the account it now reads, because another window handled the switch. It then only drops its own cached snapshot (`_usageAccountSeen`), since its bars would otherwise sit on the old numbers until the next successful scrape. A change calls `SignOutUsageWindowIfActiveAsync(pairedAccount)`, which clears the cached snapshot, signs the page out and shows a main-window info bar (`InfoBarSlot.UsageAccount`) with an "Open Claude Usage" link. It deliberately does not pop the tab, which could steal focus while the user types. The Change Account menu items pass no account, which forgets the pairing, so the CLI login that follows is adopted silently instead of being handled as a second switch.
296:- Settings-as-dialog route (v300.0): claude.ai now redirects `/settings/usage` to `/new#settings/usage` and draws settings as a fixed `role=dialog` (`cds-dialog-regions`, a grid capped at `max-height:800px`) over the chat page. Every check that compared the *path* with `/settings/usage` failed there, so `TryRedirectToUsage` took `/new` for a post-auth landing and navigated back to the usage URL every ~6.5 s (1.5 s settle + 5 s throttle) — the "keeps refreshing" report — and `TryRestoreTrim`/Refresh misjudged the page too. `ClaudeUsagePage.IsUsagePage(Uri)` (pure, `Models/ClaudeCodeModels.cs`, unit-tested) accepts either the path or the `#settings/usage` fragment and is used everywhere the C# side asks "is this the usage view"; `ClaudeUsagePage.IsAuthPath` holds the `/login`/`/logout`/`/magic-link`/`/auth` prefixes. The injected script has its own `isUsagePage()` (pathname or hash): it trims and posts snapshots only there, so a `/new` page is never trimmed or scraped. Layout: the trim CSS stretches the kept dialog to the whole viewport (`position:fixed; inset:0; max-height:none; border-radius:0; grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr)`) and hides its title row (`.col-span-full.row-start-1`, which holds claude.ai's X — closing it would leave the bare chat page); the dialog's own `overflow-y-auto` pane keeps scrolling to the end. Verified live in Edge with the extension's cookies at 1142×616.
297:- Switch Account (v301.0, replaces the v300.0 account-menu flow): `SwitchAccountButton_Click` deletes the shared cookie copy (`SharedCookiePath`, which would sign a rebuilt view back in as the same account), resets `_lastCookieSaveUtc` and navigates to `LogoutUrl` (`https://claude.ai/logout`, the `href` of claude.ai's own "Log out" menu item). `/logout` is an auth path, so `_sawSignedOutPage` is set and `TryRedirectToUsage` brings the usage view back after the next sign-in. Unlike Sign out (`SignOutAsync`, which clears all site data), the Google session stays, so Google sign-in offers the accounts it knows. With no live core it falls back to `SignOutAsync`. Why the v300.0 flow was dropped: it opened claude.ai's account menu (`[data-testid="user-menu-button"]` on `/new`) and the user's "add account" path from there is claude.ai's add/switch-account login, which locks the e-mail and disables "Continue with Google" (`disabled` when that flow is active). The switch-mode state (`_switchAccountMode`, timer, cookie signature poll, `Reload()`/redirect exceptions) went with it.
305:- Why native mode needs its own fetch: `/usage` is a TUI-only command. Measured against 3000.11.3 — `devin acp` (`available_commands_update` lists login/logout/status/…/session-stats but no `usage`) and `devin -p -- "/usage"` both answer `Unknown command: /usage`, and the CLI has no `usage` subcommand

---
name: usage-switch-account-logout-v301
description: Why Claude Usage's Switch Account clears claude.ai site data then opens /logout, and why Google sign-in was greyed out
metadata:
  type: project
---

v301.0 (2026-11-03): Switch Account navigates to https://claude.ai/logout (Daniel asked for "clica no sair"); the v300 account-menu flow was removed. The composer usage popup "Account:" shows the Claude CLI account (.claude.json oauthAccount.emailAddress) — Daniel's explicit requirement.

v302.0 (2026-11-03, commit 4412527, published): plain /logout still left Google greyed in the INSTALLED VS. It had only worked in Exp because Exp got the per-PID fallback folder `%LocalAppData%\ClaudeCodeExtension\WebView2_<pid>` (the installed VS locks the shared `WebView2` folder), i.e. a fresh profile. Fix: before /logout, delete claude.ai/anthropic.com cookies + CDP Storage.clearDataForOrigin for those origins; Google cookies kept. NOT yet verified by Daniel in the installed build.

**Why:** "works in Exp, not in published" for the Usage WebView2 usually means profile state, not code — Exp runs on a clean fallback profile whenever the main VS is open.

**How to apply:** to reproduce profile-dependent bugs, close the main VS (the Cookies file is exclusively locked, no VSS without admin) or test in Exp with the main VS closed so Exp uses the shared profile. If Google is still greyed after v302, the next suspect is Google's own cookies in the profile — try the extension's "Sair" (clears all site data). Related: [[chat-localization-v269]].

content.text:
Publiquei a versão 302.0 no Marketplace. O "Trocar de conta" agora deve deixar o "Continuar com o Google" habilitado também na versão instalada, mas isso ainda não foi testado lá.

**O que era:** o código era o mesmo, o que mudava era o navegador embutido da aba de uso:
- Com o VS normal aberto, a pasta de perfil fica travada por ele. Por isso o Exp abriu numa pasta de perfil nova e vazia, e lá tudo funcionava.
- A versão instalada usa o perfil antigo. Ele ainda guarda o estado de "adicionar conta" do claude.ai, deixado pelo "Trocar de conta" da v300. Esse estado mantém o botão do Google cinza mesmo depois do logout da v301.

**A correção:** antes de sair, o "Trocar de conta" apaga os cookies e os dados salvos só do claude.ai e do anthropic.com. Os cookies do Google ficam, então a sua conta Google continua lembrada.

**O que foi verificado:**
- No Edge headless, conferi que a limpeza apaga os dados salvos do claude.ai. Mas ela deixa alguns cookies para trás, por isso o código também apaga os cookies diretamente.
- Os 1086 testes passaram, o build Release foi feito e a publicação deu certo. O commit `4412527` já está no master.
- Não consegui reproduzir o seu caso exato: o arquivo de cookies do perfil fica travado enquanto o VS está aberto.

**Para testar:** atualize a extensão, abra o Uso do Claude e clique em **Trocar de conta** de novo. A limpeza acontece no clique.

Se o Google continuar cinza, clique em **Sair**, que apaga todos os dados do navegador embutido, inclusive os do Google. Se assim funcionar, a causa está nos cookies do próprio Google, e eu ajusto o "Trocar de conta" para limpar esses também.
